messages.subject: histograms with % of total
parts:
Hi group,

I've asked before, and found adhoc solutions to the question of how to make facetted histograms in terms of percentages. But now I have groups within each facet, and the solution seems to fail.

Specifically,

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/ggplot2/l4nrNSgxhVU


 ** y = ..count../sum(count) works for bar charts (i.e., when the
x-variable is a factor)
   ** y = k * ..density.. works for histograms (where the bins are of
fixed width k)

Any idea how the approach above can be modified to deal with multiple groups within a facet, For example:

ggplot(diamonds,aes(price,colour=color))+geom_bar(position="dodge")+facet_wrap(~cut)


Adam Loveland

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: histograms with % of total
parts:
Dodging histograms doesn't make a lot of sense since a histogram is
meant to estimate a continuous density. Using (relative) frequency
polygons makes more sense in this context, as would density estimates
with sufficient alpha transparency (as long as
the number of groups within facet is no more than three or four,
otherwise it gets cluttered). Dodging makes sense in bar charts since
the distributions are discrete.

I computed the frequencies and relative frequencies outside of ggplot2
and redid your original geom_histogram(), so I know what they should
look like. The following code that uses geom_freqpoly() appears to do
the right thing, but I didn't check it over carefully:

library(ggplot2)
library(scales) # for the percent labeller

dsmall <- diamonds[, c("cut", "color", "price")]

ggplot(dsmall, aes(x = price, color = color)) +
geom_freqpoly(aes(y = 500 * ..density..), binwidth = 500) +
facet_wrap(~ cut) +
scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
labs(x = "Price", y = "Relative frequency")

You might want to pick a color palette that is more in line with your
needs. I hope your real data has fewer subgroups to more easily
discriminate differences in distributions.

Dennis
